title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #813** asks: if every set of 7 vertices in an n-vertex graph contains a triangle, how large a clique must the graph contain? Define h(n) as this minimum guaranteed clique size. The number 7 is significant because R(3,3) = 6, so requiring a triangle in every 7-set goes beyond the Ramsey threshold.

**Status:** OPEN with progress from Erdős-Hajnal (original bounds) and Bucić-Sudakov (2023 improvement).
mathContext: This is a Ramsey-type problem connecting local triangle density to global clique structure in extremal graph theory.

title: Graph and Triangle Definitions
content:
**GraphOnN n:** A simple graph on Fin n (n vertices labeled 0..n-1).

**HasTriangle G v₁ v₂ v₃:** Vertices v₁, v₂, v₃ form a triangle (K₃) — all three are distinct and mutually adjacent.

**SubsetHasTriangle G S:** The vertex subset S contains at least one triangle.

**Every7SetHasTriangle G:** Every subset of exactly 7 vertices contains a triangle. This is the key local density condition that drives the problem.
mathContext: The number 7 is one more than R(3,3) = 6. In any 6-vertex graph, there is either a triangle or an independent set of 3. Requiring a triangle in every 7-set forces significantly more structure.

title: Cliques and the Function h(n)
content:
**IsClique G S:** Every pair of distinct vertices in S is adjacent — S forms a complete subgraph.

**HasCliqueOfSize G k:** The graph contains a clique on k vertices.

**h(n):** Axiomatized as the minimum clique size guaranteed in any n-vertex graph satisfying Every7SetHasTriangle.

**h_spec:** The specification axiom — for n ≥ 7, any graph with the local triangle property has a clique of size h(n).
mathContext: The function h(n) is defined as an extremal quantity: the minimum over all qualifying graphs of the maximum clique size. Computing it requires exhaustive search, so it is axiomatized.

title: Erdős-Hajnal Bounds
content:
**erdos_hajnal_lower_bound:** ∃ c > 0 such that h(n) ≥ c · n^{1/3} for all n ≥ 1. The lower bound means there exist graphs with small cliques but the local triangle property.

**erdos_hajnal_upper_bound:** ∃ c > 0 such that h(n) ≤ c · n^{1/2} for all n ≥ 1. The upper bound means every qualifying graph must have a clique of at least ~√n.

**erdos_hajnal_bounds (proved):** Combines both bounds into a single theorem statement, proved from the two axioms.
mathContext: The original exponent gap [1/3, 1/2] was the state of knowledge until 2023. The lower bound uses probabilistic constructions; the upper bound uses Turán-type density arguments.

title: Bucić-Sudakov Improvement (2023)
content:
**bucic_sudakov_lower_bound:** For every ε > 0, there exist c > 0 and N₀ such that h(n) ≥ c · n^{5/12-ε} for all n ≥ N₀. This captures the o(1) in the exponent.

**five_twelfths_better (proved):** 5/12 > 1/3, confirmed by norm_num.

**exponent_gap (proved):** 1/2 - 5/12 = 1/12, the remaining gap between upper and lower bounds.
mathContext: Bucić and Sudakov used algebraic and polynomial graph construction techniques to improve the lower bound. The remaining exponent gap is just 1/12.

title: The Main Conjecture
content:
**ErdosConjecture813:** Do constants c₁, c₂ > 0 exist such that:
- h(n) ≥ c₁ · n^{1/3+c₁} (strict improvement over 1/3)
- h(n) ≤ c₂ · n^{1/2-c₂} (strict improvement over 1/2)

This asks whether the polynomial exponents can be made strictly better than 1/3 and 1/2. The 2023 improvement to 5/12 provides evidence for the lower bound side but the upper bound remains at 1/2.
mathContext: Even small improvements in the exponents would be significant contributions to extremal combinatorics.

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_813** packages the two main known results:
1. ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, h(n) ≥ c · n^{1/3} (Erdős-Hajnal lower bound)
2. ∃ c > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, h(n) ≤ c · n^{1/2} (Erdős-Hajnal upper bound)

Proved by `⟨erdos_hajnal_lower_bound, erdos_hajnal_upper_bound⟩`.

**Status:** OPEN — the exact growth rate of h(n) is unknown.
mathContext: The summary theorem captures the essential state of knowledge. The Bucić-Sudakov improvement refines the lower bound but the original Erdős-Hajnal bounds remain the cleanest statement.
